bill.title: National Plan for Epilepsy Act
bill.latestActionText: Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions. Ordered to be reported with an amendment in the nature of a substitute favorably.

industries.rationale: The bill's focus on epilepsy treatment, diagnosis, and cure research directly affects pharmaceutical and medical device companies developing epilepsy therapies.
The national plan's coordination of epilepsy care and services would affect hospitals and health systems that diagnose and treat epilepsy patients.

bill.plainSummary: This bill directs the Department of Health and Human Services to create and carry out a national plan to address epilepsy, including prevention, diagnosis, treatment, and research coordination across federal agencies. HHS must establish an advisory council that reports to Congress every two years and must itself submit annual progress reports with recommended actions. These requirements would remain in effect until the end of 2035.

plain.whoItTouches: People with an illness that is still being studied. Anyone whose personal data is held by a company.

bill.title: Keeping All Students Safe Act
bill.latestActionText: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions.

industries.rationale: The bill directly regulates schools and Head Start programs, imposing new training requirements, compliance procedures, and enforcement obligations on educational institutions.
The bill creates a new private right of action for students subjected to unlawful seclusion or restraint, which would generate litigation opportunities.

bill.plainSummary: This bill would prohibit schools and Head Start programs that receive federal funding from using seclusion (confining a student alone in a locked room) and would restrict the use of physical restraints to situations where a student poses an imminent danger of serious physical injury. It requires staff training in crisis intervention, establishes procedures for reporting incidents, and creates enforcement mechanisms including the ability for students to sue and for federal agencies to withhold payments from programs that violate the rules. The bill also provides grants to help state education agencies implement these policies.

plain.whoItTouches: Students, teachers, and the families paying for it.

bill.title: A joint resolution to direct the removal of United States Armed Forces from hostilities within or against the Republic of Cuba that have not been authorized by Congress.
bill.latestActionText: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Foreign Relations.

industries.rationale: The resolution would directly affect military deployment decisions and operational scope for defense contractors supporting U.S. forces in the region.

bill.plainSummary: This joint resolution would require the President to withdraw U.S. military forces from any hostilities in or against Cuba unless Congress has formally declared war or authorized the use of force. The measure includes exceptions allowing the U.S. to defend itself from attack or imminent attack, and to continue lawful counternarcotics operations. It addresses the constitutional balance between executive and legislative authority over military deployments.

plain.whoItTouches: Mostly people outside the United States. It reaches most readers here only indirectly.
